title: TRA Risk Scheme
description: Practical impact/likelihood scheme combining a Bug Bar impact rubric (max C/I/A/Safety) with a decomposed likelihood = Exposure x Exploitability (interview participant P11), on a 5x5 matrix. Inspired by Fockel/Phoenix Contact (Bug Bar + CVSS), Loepz 5x5 matrix, and CRA/IEC 62443 expectations.

scale.label: Very Low
scale.desc: Physical access plus rare expertise needed; mature controls; no known path.

scale.label: Low
scale.desc: Local access and specialist skill; controls present; limited public knowledge.

scale.label: Medium
scale.desc: Adjacent/local access, moderate skill; partial controls; known technique.

scale.label: High
scale.desc: Remote or easy local access, common skill; weak controls; public exploit/tooling.

scale.label: Very High
scale.desc: Remote, low skill, scalable; no effective control; trivial or automated.

likelihood.derivation: Likelihood = round(sqrt(Exposure x Exploitability)) mapped to 1-5; Risk = Likelihood x Impact on the 5x5 matrix. This realises interview participant P11's Exposure/Exploitability/Impact intuition (P11 found a single coarse likelihood insufficient) while keeping the familiar matrix. Exposure = attack-surface reachability of the entry interface (higher = more reachable); Exploitability = ease of exploitation once reached (higher = easier). The referenced attacker profile is a feasibility GATE, not an averaged term: the threat's required attacker capability is (6 - exploitability), expressed on the same 1-5 capability scale as the attacker profile, and the attacker's own capability must meet or exceed it (equivalently capability + exploitability >= 6); its access must also be proximate enough for the exposure. Control maturity is excluded because controls act on the residual risk, not the inherent likelihood (avoids double-counting).

scale.label: Negligible
scale.desc: No safety effect; minor data exposure; self-recovering.

scale.label: Minor
scale.desc: Local CIA loss; nuisance; bounded process disturbance.

scale.label: Moderate
scale.desc: Process value falsification or downtime; reputational; no safety harm.

scale.label: Major
scale.desc: Loss of control/view of overfill protection; potential SIL demotion; multi-site.

scale.label: Severe
scale.desc: Safety hazard (overfill, spill); environmental/human harm; fleet-wide.

impact.rule: Impact = max(C, I, A, Safety) for the worst plausible asset, defaulting to the binding safety case (PR-04).

cvss.role: Supplementary signal that may inform the exploitability factor of the likelihood (Fockel / Phoenix Contact, TUV-certified). Not the primary risk model.
cvss.suggestion: exploitability is estimated from the CVSS v3 exploitability metrics (AC/PR/UI) in the vector, NOT the base score (which includes the impact sub-score and would double-count the Bug Bar impact).

attackTree.description: Optional per-threat attack-defense tree (Kordy et al. 2010; Jhawar et al. 2015). Gates: AND, OR, SAND (sequential AND). Defences attach as countermeasure nodes.
